title: MCP servers P0: config, stdio transport, and search_tool/use_tool in the shell

AC1.note: config.test.ts + config.schema-parity.test.ts (29 tests). Project-beats-user merge asserted on loadMcpServers directly; the cwd→git-root walk asserted with a fixture nested two directories deep (projectConfigFiles); overlay and ${VAR}/${VAR:-default} expansion asserted at load. Round-tripped through the READER in store.test.ts, not just re-read as JSON.

AC2.note: stdio.live.test.ts, gated block. RAN against the real @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem fetched by npx: status connected, non-zero tool count, 7 pass with KERYX_ALLOW_REAL_SUBPROCESS=1. Gated and excluded from CI per the keryx-mcp-client precedent; the gating is recorded in the file header rather than the criterion dropped.

AC3.note: BOTH halves: catalog.test.ts asserts the over-long/invalid FQN is absent from entries, and doctor.test.ts asserts doctor lists it as skipped WITH the reason (formatDoctorReport output checked too). Mutation: dropping the skipped array fails the doctor test. Real-world instance found by pointing doctor at keryx serve-mcp — 26 skipped, recorded as D-13.

AC4.note: mcp-tool-surface.test.ts, asserted against buildInteractiveAgentTools output — the definitions the agent actually gets, not the catalog. search_tool and use_tool present; none of the three FQNs present. Also: without a runtime the pair is absent entirely, and adding one adds exactly two. shell.test.ts's exact TUI tool-name list now includes both. Mutation: registering the pair unconditionally fails two tests.

AC5.note: stdio.live.test.ts against a REAL fixture MCP server over stdio, no network (fixtures/mcp-servers/echo-server.ts, hand-rolled JSON-RPC so a framing bug cannot cancel out against the SDK on both sides). search_tool returns fx__echo; use_tool performs tools/call and returns the content the other process produced; result marked untrusted. Handshake and tools/list asserted separately.

AC6.note: Two levels. tools.test.ts asserts the cap CONSTANT itself (MAX_TOOL_RESULT_BYTES === 20_000) so a silently raised cap fails rather than passes. stdio.live.test.ts makes a real server return 40,000 bytes and asserts the model-visible output carries the truncation marker and stays under cap+200.

AC7.note: All three arms driven through runAgentTurn — the REAL gate, not a substitute (mcp-tool-surface.test.ts). ask: requestApproval called with use_tool, server reached only after yes; refusal: server never reached; trust: STILL asks; headless (no requestApproval): denied, no call. Anti-vacuity: auto mode does NOT ask — that test caught my first attempt passing permissionMode on the wrong object, which had made the other three assert ask-mode four times. NOTE: implemented WITHOUT a per-tool approval layer. My first cut added approveMcpCall inside use_tool; D-05 forbids a fourth decision layer and it would have double-prompted, since use_tool's static destructive risk already routes every call through resolveApprovalDecision. Deleted. classifyToolRisk is now advisory output in search_tool hits only — de-escalating on a third-party readOnlyHint is precisely what ADR-0009 forbids.

AC8.note: Twice. runtime.test.ts: two configured servers, one connect throws — good is connected with its tools in the catalog, bad is failed with the message, createMcpRuntime never throws and never blocks (asserted: it returns with the dial outstanding). stdio.live.test.ts: same shape with a command that genuinely does not exist, so the failure comes from the OS rather than the test. Malformed config also carried, not thrown.

AC9.note: runtime.test.ts, both routes to disabled (file enabled:false, and personal overlay). The ABSENCE OF THE PROCESS is asserted directly — a dial counter that must be 0 — not inferred from the reported status. Plus an anti-vacuity test that an enabled server IS dialled, so the counter can move. store.test.ts asserts disable leaves the config file intact, and byte-identical for a committed project file.

AC10.note: constraints.test.ts: CAPABILITY_REGISTRY holds no id containing 'mcp', asserted against the real imported array; plus a non-empty check so the filter is not vacuous; plus no file in src/mcp-servers/ imports capability/ at all.

AC11.note: constraints.test.ts, each checked rather than asserted. No static @modelcontextprotocol/sdk import in any production file here, AND the stronger end-to-end form: 'bun src/cli.ts mcp --help' is spawned and must exit 0. No foreign config path named in code (mcp.config.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .claude.json, .mcp.json) — comments stripped first, so a file is not failed for documenting the rule it obeys. Store writes only via userConfigFile/projectConfigFile/overlayFile. No Codex import (D-12). connectCodexMcpClient/gatedSuperviseCodexMcpRun suites still green in the full run. Bare 'keryx mcp' still serves: mcp.ts routes only the six consumer verbs and leaves the no-subcommand path on serveMcpCommand; mcp-servers.test.ts asserts serve/install/uninstall are NOT claimed by the consumer surface.

AC12.note: All four from SOURCE, none from the installed binary. bun test: 8623 pass / 19 skip / 0 fail. bunx tsc --noEmit: clean. bun run lint: clean. bun src/cli.ts skills verify --bundled: pass. One order-dependent flake observed in src/sac/session-wrap-up.test.ts on an earlier full run (passes in isolation and on re-run, untouched by this work) — recorded, not silently ignored.

tasks.title: Collect remaining context
tasks.dispositionReason: Context was the package itself: specification.md §2-§5, implementation-plan.md P0 items 1-8, decisions.md D-01..D-12. D-05 in particular decided the approval design, after a first cut violated it.

tasks.title: Implement per plan
tasks.dispositionReason: All 8 P0 items, plus the shell wiring item 5 required and I had initially skipped. New modules: config, store, catalog, manager, tools, doctor, runtime, spawn-env; CLI in src/commands/mcp-servers.ts routed from mcp.ts.

tasks.title: Add/adjust tests and make them pass
tasks.dispositionReason: 191 tests across 12 files in src/mcp-servers/ + src/commands/. Includes a real stdio fixture server, a flag-gated real-npx run, and the agent gate driven through runAgentTurn. 13 mutations applied and all 13 killed by the tests that name them.

tasks.title: Self-review and prepare draft PR
tasks.dispositionReason: Self-review found two real defects in my own work, both fixed before the PR left draft: (1) the tool pair had zero production callers — built and tested but never wired, so AC4/AC8/AC9 could not have been met; (2) the in-tool approval gate violated D-05's 'no fourth decision layer' and would have double-prompted, while adding de-escalation on a third-party readOnlyHint that ADR-0009 forbids. PR #522 ready for review, CI green.
